{{Medal|Bronze|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|2012 São Sebastião do Paraíso]]|[[Canada men's national basketball team|National team]]}} }} '''Andrew Christian Wiggins''' (born February 23, 1995) is a Canadian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Miami Heat]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was selected with the [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]] in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] after one year of [[college basketball]] with the [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]. Wiggins grew up in Canada before attending his last two years of high school in the United States, where he was named a [[McDonald's All-American]]. At Kansas, he was named a second-team consensus [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] before becoming the second Canadian to be selected No. 1 overall in an NBA draft. After a preseason trade to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], Wiggins earned [[NBA Rookie of the Year]] honors for the 2014–15 season. After five-and-a-half seasons with Minnesota, he was traded to Golden State in 2020. In 2022, Wiggins won his first [[NBA championship]] and was selected for his first [[NBA All-Star]] game, and was named a [[Western Conference (NBA)|Western Conference]] starter. He has also been a member of the [[Canada men's national basketball team|Canadian national team]]. ==Early life== Wiggins was born in [[Toronto|Toronto, Ontario]]{{cite news |last=Blair, Jeff 23, a three-team trade was completed involving the Cavaliers, the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] and the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. As part of the deal, Wiggins and Bennett were traded to the Wolves, along with [[Thaddeus Young]], then of the Sixers. |access-date=November 9, 2016}} Five days later, he set a new career high with '''47 points''' in a 125–99 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], becoming the first Canadian-born player to score 40-plus |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900248 |title=Wiggins' 40 points leads T-Wolves over Nuggets 112-99 |work=ESPN.com |date=February 15, 2017 |access-date=February 16, 2017}} On February 24, he scored 27 points in a 97–84 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]], topping 20 points for the 16th straight game, tying a franchise record.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900268 |title=Towns, Wiggins help Wolves beat Mavericks 97-84 |work=ESPN.com |date=February 24, 2017 |access-date=February 25, 2017}} ==== First playoff The last time Wiggins was inactive was November 10, 2015, when he sat out a loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] because of a sore right knee.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070736 |title=Leonard scores 35, Raptors beat Wolves 112-105 to reach 5-0 |work=ESPN.com |date=October 24, 2018 |access-date=October 24, 2018}} Wiggins returned to action on October 31 against the [[Utah Jazz]] after missing three games.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070788 |title=Rose scores career-high 50 as Timberwolves top Jazz 128-125 |work=ESPN.com |date=October 31, 2018 |access-date=October 31, 2018}} He struggled early in the season, culminating in an 0-for-12 shooting night on November 24 against the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070962 |title=Karl-Anthony Towns picks up slack, carries Wolves past Bulls |work=ESPN.com |date=November 24, 2018 |access-date=December 5, 2018 |quote=Wiggins was scoreless on 0-for-12 shooting.}}{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071043 |title=Towns has 35 points, Timberwolves beat Hornets 121-104 |work=ESPN.com |date=December 5, 2018 |access-date=December 5, 2018}} It was the first time in his career he finished a game scoreless. Spurs beat Wolves 116-113 |work=ESPN.com |date=January 18, 2019 |access-date=January 18, 2019}} On January 27, he scored a game-high 35 points in a 125–111 loss to the Jazz.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071413 |title=Mitchell scores 29 to lead Jazz past Timberwolves 125-111 |work=ESPN.com |date=January 27, 2019 |access-date=June 20, 2019}} On January 18, 2020, Wiggins achieved his first career [[triple-double]] with 18 points, 10 rebounds and a career-high 11 assists.{{cite web |url=https://www.startribune.com/andrew-wiggins-first-triple-double-not-enough-for-wolves-vs-toronto/567115132/ |title=Wiggins' first triple-double not enough for Wolves vs. Toronto |last=Youngblood |first=Kent |website=StarTribune |date=January 19, 2020 |access-date=December 8, 2021}} ===Golden State Warriors (2020–2025)=== ==== First year in Golden State and play-in appearance (2020–2021) ==== On February 6, 2020, Wiggins and two draft picks were traded to the [[Golden State Warriors]] in exchange for [[Jacob Evans]], [[D'Angelo Russell]] and [[Omari Spellman]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-acquire-wiggins-20200206 |title=Warriors Acquire Andrew Wiggins & 2021 First and Second Round Draft Picks From Minnesota |work=NBA.com |date=February 6, 2020}} Wiggins scored 24 points and had five steals in his debut for the Warriors, in a 125–120 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |last=Friedell |first=Nick |date=February 9, 2020 |title=Andrew Wiggins scores 24 points in debut with Warriors |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/28662875 |access-date=December 8, 2021 |website=ESPN.com}} The Warriors failed to qualify for the playoffs and finished with a 15–50 record, the worst in the league. On March 19, 2021, Wiggins scored a season-high 40 points, alongside eight rebounds, four assists and four steals, in a 116–103 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web |last=Bailey |first=Clay |date=March 20, 2021 |title=Wiggins scores 40 as short-handed Warriors beat Grizzlies |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000636 |access-date=June 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} The Warriors qualified for the newly implemented play-in tournament; however, they suffered two straight losses to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and [[Memphis Grizzlies]], failing to reach the postseason for the second straight season despite a 22-point, 10-rebound [[double-double]] from Wiggins in their loss to the Grizzlies.{{Cite web |last=McCauley |first=Janie |date=May 23, 2021 |title=Morant, Grizzlies beat Warriors in OT, advance to face Jazz |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0052000211 |access-date=June 14, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} ==== First All-Star selection and NBA championship (2021–2022) ==== On December 6, 2021, Wiggins scored 28 points on a career-high eight threes made, in a 126–95 win over the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web |url=https://clutchpoints.com/warriors-news-andrew-wiggins-epic-transformation-will-make-stephen-curry-proud/ |title=Andrew Wiggins' epic transformation with Warriors will make Stephen Curry proud |last=Guinhawa |first=Angelo |website=ClutchPoints |date=December 6, 2021 |access-date=December 8, 2021}} On January 27, 2022, he was named a Western Conference starter for the [[2022 NBA All-Star Game]], his first [[List of NBA All-Stars|All-Star]] selection.{{Cite web |title=Steph joined by Wiggins as NBA All-Star Game starters |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/warriors-steph-curry-andrew-wiggins-named-nba-all-star-game-starters |access-date=January 27, 2022 |website=NBC Sports |date=January 27, 2022}} He received support in the form of fan voting points from [[K-pop]] star, [[BamBam]], who provided a strategic [[social media]] boost.{{cite news |title=Wiggins owes assist to K-pop star Bam Bam for All-Star selection |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nba/news/wiggins-owes-assist-to-k-pop-star-bam-bam-for-all-star-selection |work=NBC Sports |date=29 January 2022}} He was the third first-time All-Star to be voted a starter in his eighth season or later.{{efn|The first two were [[Bob Boozer]] (eighth season, [[1968 NBA All-Star Game|1968]]) and [[Kyle Lowry]] (ninth, [[2015 NBA All-Star Game|2015]]){{cite news |first=Tim |last=Bontemps |title=LeBron James, Kevin Durant named captains again for All-Star Game as starter pool announced |date=January 28, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33161755 |access-date=January 29, 2022}}}} Wiggins also became the first No. 1 overall draft pick in the modern draft era (since [[1966 NBA draft|1966]]) to earn his first All-Star selection in his eighth season or later. On May 22, during Game 3 of the [[2022 NBA playoffs|Western Conference Finals]], Wiggins scored a playoff career-high 27 points and tied his then-playoff career high with 11 rebounds in a 109–100 Game 3 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web |last=Dixon |first=Schuyler |date=May 23, 2022 |title=Warriors overcome Luka's 40, seize 3-0 series lead |url=https://www.nba.com/game/gsw-vs-dal-0042100313 |access-date=May 23, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} [[File:Andrew Wiggins warming up with the Heat during the 2024-25 season..jpg|alt=Andrew Wiggins warming up with the Heat during the 2024-25 season.|thumb|479x479px|Andrew Wiggins warming up with the [[Miami Heat|Heat]] during the [[2024–25 Miami Heat season|2024-25 season]].]] In Game 4 of the [[2022 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], Wiggins posted a 17-point, 16-rebound (a playoff career high) double-double in a 107–97 win over the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web |date=June 11, 2022 |title=Curry scores 43 to beat Boston, Warriors tie NBA Finals 2-2 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401442533 |access-date=June 14, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |agency=AP}} In Game 5, he logged a 26-point, 13-rebound double-double in a 104–94 win. Wiggins won his first [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] after the Warriors defeated the Celtics in six games. He finished the NBA Finals as the leading rebounder, blocker and second highest scorer for the Warriors after averaging 18.3 points, 8.8 rebounds and 1.5 blocks per game, along with playing stifling defense on Boston [[All-NBA]] forward [[Jayson Tatum]].{{Cite web |date=June 14, 2022 |title=Wiggins delivers on both ends, Warriors lead NBA Finals 3-2 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401442534 |access-date=June 14, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |agency=AP}}{{Cite magazine |title=Jayson Tatum's Old Tweet About Andrew Wiggins Goes Viral After Game 5 |url=https://www.si.com/extra-mustard/2022/06/14/jayson-tatum-old-tweet-andrew-wiggins-viral-game-5-jabari-parker |access-date=June 14, 2022 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 14, 2022}}{{cite web |title=Poole, Wiggins come to hilarious realization after Finals win |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/jordan-poole-andrew-wiggins-hilarious-realization-after-nba-finals-win |website=RSN |date=June 17, 2022 |access-date=17 June 2022 |language=en}} ==== Contract extension (2022–2025) ==== On October 15, 2022, Wiggins signed a four-year contract extension worth $109 million with the Warriors.{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |last2=Andrews |first2=Kendra |author-link2=Kendra Andrews |name-list-style=and |date=2022-10-15 |title=Wiggins, Warriors agree to 4-year, $109M deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34802456 |access-date=2022-10-15 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} On November 20, Wiggins scored 22 points on 6-of-11 shooting from three-point range. |url=https://clutchpoints.com/warriors-news-stephen-curry-klay-thompson-andrew-wiggins-set-unreal-3pt-record-never-seen-before |title=Stephen Curry, Klay Thompson, Andrew Wiggins set unreal 3pt record
